//! Aggregated OpenAPI document for the `/api/v1/*` surface and its
//! HTTP serving handler.
//!
//! K7 split: pulled out of `v1/mod.rs` so the orchestrator stays under
//! the 600 LOC ceiling as the schema registry grows. Adding a new typed
//! handler still follows the cadence documented at the top of
//! `v1/mod.rs`:
//!
//!   1. Annotate the handler with `#[utoipa::path(...)]`.
//!   2. Register the function in `ApiDoc::paths(...)` below.
//!   3. Register any request/response structs in `components(schemas(...))`.
//!   4. Mount the route in `public_router()` or `protected_router()`
//!      back in `mod.rs`.
//!
//! Re-exported from `v1::*` so callers see the same symbol name.

use axum::{response::IntoResponse, Json};
use utoipa::OpenApi;

use super::*;

pub struct ApiDoc;

/// Serve the OpenAPI document describing the `/api/v1/*` surface.
///
/// The current emitter (utoipa 4 with axum 0.7) produces an OpenAPI 3.0.3
/// document. The rewrite plan calls for 3.1, which requires bumping to
/// utoipa 5 + axum 0.8 — that upgrade is folded into a later cleanup pass
/// since the type-generator we use (`@hey-api/openapi-ts`)
/// accepts both 3.0 and 3.1 specs without behavior change.
pub async fn serve_openapi() -> impl IntoResponse {
    Json(ApiDoc::openapi())
}
